chapter_title: 1. LLM Runtime Fundamentals for Agent Engineers
audit: The consultant analogy identifies separate responsibilities but does not let the reader inspect the actual contents of a call or a rejected proposal. Lesson A places a specific order, current payment evidence, required continuation reference and execution restrictions in separate containers. It makes selective context and retained state visible without claiming every endpoint is stateless. Lesson B presents a syntactically valid refund request against a smaller remaining balance and missing approval. The reader must distinguish parsing success, domain failure and deferred authority. Together the lessons expose why plausible structured text cannot establish a financial result.

lessons.title: What goes into this consultation?
lessons.intro: ShopAssist prepares a second consultation about ORD-104233. The first lookup found two captures; no refund has been approved.

relations: The call folder selects retained, permitted facts.
Action checks apply to every proposed operation.

read: Inspect the payment identifiers supplied to this call.
The continuation reference stays in the runtime, where the adapter can preserve required provider items.
The action desk decides whether a proposal may execute.
lessons.question: If the next folder omits OBS-7, may the model assume the duplicate captures still exist?
lessons.answer: No. The runtime should supply the retained observation or obtain current records. Training knowledge and a fluent continuation cannot establish this order's payment state. Provider continuation may help preserve protocol state, but it does not replace application evidence or authorization.
lessons.takeaway: A call receives selected evidence; authority remains outside the generated response.
lessons.assumption: Fictional records; folder contents simplify serialized context. Provider continuation requirements vary, and the consultant analogy supplies no human accountability.

lessons.title: A valid request can still fail
lessons.intro: A complete model response proposes a USD 24.99 refund. PAY-B has only USD 14.99 remaining after an earlier partial refund.

data.name: Refund proposal RF-12

checks.label: Approval
checks.detail: No approval for this exact proposal

data.result: Do not dispatch; correct and re-evaluate the proposal

read: The integer is valid even though its financial meaning fails.
The remaining balance comes from the payment service.
Approval cannot repair an amount that violates the balance rule.
lessons.question: If approval arrives for 2499 minor units, can RF-12 execute unchanged?
lessons.answer: No. Approval is only one independent condition. The requested amount still exceeds the current refundable balance. Create a valid proposal, check fresh preconditions, and obtain approval bound to its exact effect before dispatch.
lessons.takeaway: Schema, current business rules and authority are independent gates.
lessons.assumption: Fictional complete response and payment records; amounts are exact USD minor units. No payment has been dispatched.
